components.css: .ds-session { margin: 0; background: #15171c; color: #ecece6; font: 400 14px/1.85 "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; font-variant-ligatures: none; } .ds-session-bar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid #2c3038; font-size: 12.5px; color: #a9adb6; } .ds-session-lines { margin: 0; padding: 18px 20px 6px; list-style: none; } .ds-session-lines li { position: relative; padding-left: 30px; } .ds-session-lines li::before { position: absolute; left: 0; color: #6b7080; } .ds-session-lines .c::before { content: ">"; } .ds-session-lines .s::before { content: "<"; } .ds-session-lines .s { color: #8fd3c4; } .ds-session-lines .held { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; background: rgba(178, 58, 48, 0.16); margin-inline: -20px; padding-inline: 50px 20px; } .ds-session-lines .held::before, .ds-session-lines .loop::before { left: 20px; } .ds-session-lines del { text-decoration-color: #e46a5f; text-decoration-thickness: 1.5px; color: #c9ccd3; } .ds-flag { flex: none; align-self: center; font: 600 11px/1 "Schibsted Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ff9a8f; border: 1px solid currentColor; padding: 4px 6px 3px; } .ds-session-lines .loop { margin-top: 10px; margin-inline: -20px; padding-inline: 50px 20px; background: rgba(64, 196, 170, 0.14); color: #b6eee0; } .ds-session-foot { margin: 12px 0 0; padding: 12px 20px 16px; border-top: 1px solid #2c3038; font: 400 15px "Schibsted Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif; color: #a9adb6; } .ds-session-foot strong { color: #fff; }

narrative.overview:
SMTPMonster looks like the documentation of a piece of infrastructure, not the homepage of a side project. The ground is off-white paper, the text is near-black ink, and the proof is the protocol itself: SMTP sessions, credential tables, `.env` blocks and inbox rows set in monospace, presented as facts rather than illustrations. Prose sits beside them in a precise grotesk, tightly tracked at display sizes, plain at reading sizes.

The world is flat, square and ruled. Structure comes from one-pixel rules, alternating paper tones and full-bleed ink bands, never from cards with rounded corners or soft drop shadows. Colour carries meaning, not decoration: one teal signal for "held, looped back, yours", one muted red strike for recipients who never get the mail. The horned teal monster is the mark (nav, favicon, close, the sender avatar on a looped message) and stays small and confident; it is never blown up into a hero illustration.

Motion is spare and grammatical: protocol lines reveal once, line by line, on an expo-out ease, and colour changes on hover in 0.2s. Nothing bounces, nothing loops.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground, ink text, slate secondary text; colour reserved for meaning.
Every protocol fact (host, port, command, header, env var) is monospace; everything else is the grotesk.
Square corners everywhere; the only circle is the mascot avatar.
One-pixel rules divide content; an ink rule closes each section head.
Full-bleed ink bands for terminal output and the LogMonster section.
A recurring 5:6 two-column split, collapsing to one column at 960px.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal means held, looped back, or "act here". It is never a decorative fill, a section background, or a gradient.

rules.name: The Strike Is Not an Accent Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for undelivered recipients and errors. If nothing failed or was held, there is no red on the screen.

rules.name: The Protocol Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Hosts, ports, commands, headers, addresses in a session and env vars are set in the mono with ligatures off. Prose about them stays in the grotesk.

rules.name: The Ruled, Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Separate content with a one-pixel rule or a tone change. A shadow is reserved for an object that is itself a document.

dos: Do put every protocol fact in the mono with ligatures off, on ink for live output and on card white for reference data.
Do separate content with 1px rules and tone shifts (paper, paper shade, card, ink).
Do keep teal for held, looped-back and actionable states, and strike red for undelivered recipients and errors.
Do close each section head with a 1px ink rule under a 5:6 headline/intro split.
Do keep the monster small: 28 to 40px in chrome, 72 to 96px at most as a closing mark.
Do reveal protocol output once, line by line on the expo-out ease, and show it complete under reduced motion.
donts: Don't round corners on buttons, fields, panels or tables; the avatar disc is the only circle.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or buttons; only a document shown as an artefact is lifted.
Don't use teal or red as decorative fills, gradients or section backgrounds.
Don't turn the monster into a large cartoon hero illustration.
Don't add bounces, loops or attention-seeking motion.
